function.name: generate_image_tool
function.description: Generates an image based on the provided description and saves it with the specified file name. The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.name: tts_tool
function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The text content that needs to be converted to speech.

speaker.description: The voice to be used for the text-to-speech conversion.

file_name.description: The name of the file to save the audio output without the extension. If left empty, a default name will be generated based on the content.

function.name: write_markdown_tool
function.description: Writes the provided content to a Markdown (.md) file on the disk. This function should be used when there is a need to persist text data in Markdown format as a result of a user action or a process that requires saving information in a structured text file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: write_html_tool
function.description: Writes an HTML file to disk with the given content. Ensures HTML tags within the content are properly closed. This function should be used when there is a need to save HTML content to a file as part of a 'save' operation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

Here’s a quick rundown of the most common tools, APIs, and platforms you can use to book flights—whether you’re building a travel app, automating a booking workflow, or just looking for the best way to find and reserve seats.

| Category | Tool / Service | What it offers | Typical use case |
|----------|----------------|----------------|------------------|
| **Flight Search & Booking APIs** | **Amadeus for Developers** | Comprehensive flight search, booking, and ancillary services. Includes seat availability, fare rules, and dynamic pricing. | Enterprise travel apps, corporate booking portals. |
| | **Skyscanner API** | Search for flights, hotels, car rentals. Provides price alerts and multi-city itineraries. | Consumer travel sites, price comparison widgets. |
| | **Google Flights API (via Google Travel)** | Flight search, price history, and itinerary suggestions. (Note: Google’s public API is limited; many use unofficial wrappers.) | Integrations with Google services, travel assistants. |
| | **Expedia Rapid API** | Search, book, and manage flights, hotels, car rentals. Offers loyalty program integration. | Travel agencies, OTA aggregators. |
| | **Kayak API** | Flight search, price alerts, and booking via partner networks. | Price comparison sites, travel blogs. |
| | **Travelport Universal API** | Global distribution system (GDS) access for flights, hotels, car rentals. | Large travel agencies, corporate travel solutions. |
| | **Sabre API** | GDS-level flight inventory, booking, and ancillary services. | Enterprise travel, airline partners. |
| | **OpenSky API** | Real‑time flight data (positions, status). Not for booking but useful for flight tracking. | Flight tracking apps, aviation analytics. |
| | **FlightAware API** | Flight status, delay predictions, historical data. | Flight status widgets, travel alerts. |
| | **FlightStats API** | Flight status, airport data, delay analytics. | Travel apps needing real‑time status. |
| | **AirLabs API** | Flight search, booking, and flight status. | Small to medium travel startups. |
| | **Travelpayouts API** | Affiliate flight search and booking. | Affiliate marketing, travel blogs. |
| | **CheapOair API** | Flight search and booking with commission model. | Affiliate sites, travel agencies. |
| | **Trip.com API** | Flight, hotel, and train booking. | Global travel platforms. |
| | **Priceline API** | Flight search and booking. | Travel agencies, corporate booking. |
| | **Orbitz API** | Flight, hotel, car rental booking. | Travel agencies, corporate travel. |
| | **Travelocity API** | Flight, hotel, car rental booking. | Travel agencies, corporate travel. |
| | **Booking.com API** | Primarily hotels, but offers flight booking via partners. | Hotel-focused travel sites. |
| | **Airbnb API** | Not for flights, but useful for accommodation. | Travel apps combining lodging and flights. |
| | **OpenTravel API** | Open-source flight search and booking. | DIY travel solutions, research. |
| | **FlightRadar24 API** | Real‑time flight tracking. | Flight tracking widgets. |
| | **FlightAware Firehose** | Streaming flight data. | Real‑time analytics, flight tracking. |
| | **FlightStats Global API** | Flight status, airport data. | Travel apps needing status updates. |
| | **FlightLabs API** | Flight search and booking. | Small travel startups. |

### Quick‑start checklist for building a flight‑booking flow

1. **Choose an API**  
   - For a consumer‑facing app: Skyscanner, Amadeus, or Travelpayouts.  
   - For enterprise or corporate: Sabre, Amadeus, or Travelport.  
   - For affiliate revenue: CheapOair, Travelpayouts, or Expedia Rapid.

2. **Register & Get Credentials**  
   - Sign up on the provider’s developer portal.  
   - Obtain API keys / OAuth tokens.

3. **Search Flights**  
   - Use the “search” endpoint with parameters: origin, destination, departure date, return date, cabin class, number of passengers, etc.  
   - Most APIs return a list of itineraries with fares, airlines, layovers, and availability.

4. **Select an Itinerary**  
   - Show the user options (price, duration, number of stops).  
   - Optionally filter by airline, price range, or travel time.

5. **Book the Flight**  
   - Call the “booking” endpoint with passenger details, payment info, and selected itinerary ID.  
   - Handle payment processing (many APIs support direct payment or redirect to a payment gateway).

6. **Confirm & Store**  
   - Receive a booking confirmation (PNR, ticket number).  
   - Store the booking details in your database for future reference or cancellations.

7. **Handle Cancellations / Modifications**  
   - Use the “cancellation” or “modification” endpoints if supported.  
   - Update your records accordingly.

8. **Integrate Ancillary Services** (optional)  
   - Add baggage, seat selection, travel insurance, or car rentals via the same API or partner APIs.

### Helpful Resources

- **Amadeus for Developers** – https://developers.amadeus.com  
- **Skyscanner API** – https://partners.skyscanner.net  
- **Travelport Universal API** – https://developer.travelport.com  
- **Sabre APIs** – https://developer.sabre.com  
- **Expedia Rapid API** – https://developer.expediagroup.com  
- **Travelpayouts API** – https://travelpayouts.com/api  

Feel free to let me know which specific provider you’re interested in, and I can dive deeper into its endpoints, authentication flow, or sample code snippets!
